clue.text: Loud shrieking comes from this bird

indicators.note: the bird's name is said to come out of the letters, so they are rearranged to produce it

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noisy screech is heard from some bird.
explanation.walkthrough: F joins the letters of SHRIEKING and 'comes from' rearranges the ten letters; the bird is actually noted for its piercing call.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly coloured river-diving species, so a straightforward example of a bird.

clue.text: Firm rule about the French salad

indicators.note: the firm and rule pieces sit around the French article, enclosing it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a law is a rule
LES is French for 'the' (plural)

explanation.surface: A company regulation concerning French salad.
explanation.definitionFit: A shredded cabbage dish dressed with mayonnaise, served as a side salad.

clue.text: Confront with small account charge

parts.note: AC is the short form of account
a cost is a charge or price

explanation.surface: Someone challenges a trader over a minor bill and fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach and address someone boldly is to confront them, often aggressively.

clue.text: Up-beat game

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to flog is to beat

explanation.surface: A cheerful, upbeat sporting pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up-beat' looks like the adjective meaning cheerful; split, it tells you to reverse a word for beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport played with clubs on a course, so it is a kind of game.

clue.text: Staggers, due to ill-fitting satin shoes

indicators.note: shoes that fit badly are out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone totters about because their satin shoes don't fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggers' tempts as a verb of walking unsteadily; here it means amazes.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to amaze them, a synonym in the sense of shocking.

clue.text: Part of the deal, perhaps, sounds incomplete

indicators.note: signals that a phrase spoken aloud gives the answer's sound

parts.note: something incomplete is not whole

explanation.surface: Part of a business deal seems unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is also pine or fir timber: a hole left where a knot fell out is part of a deal plank. 'Perhaps' flags this as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap in timber where a knot was, found in a deal board as one example.

clue.text: Spring vegetable

definitions.meaning: to spring up is to grow or shoot
a Brussels ... is a green vegetable

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to shoot up; as a noun it is the small green brassica.

clue.text: A slight incoherence in speech

explanation.definitionFit: Both an insulting remark and a blurred way of speaking, two senses of one word.

clue.text: Award for Brand X

parts.note: a branding iron is used to brand cattle
the letter X is a cross

explanation.surface: A prize given to a product called Brand X.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand X' reads as an anonymous product in an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A German military decoration for bravery, hence an award.

clue.text: Penal settlement in the country

indicators.note: the letters settle into a new order, signalling an anagram

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prison colony set up somewhere in the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penal settlement' reads as a convict colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A Himalayan nation between India and China.

clue.text: Ceases to be in love, leaves

explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for both losing affection and departing, two idiomatic senses.

clue.text: Excel, getting gold in some sort of sports

definitions.note: an adjective describing a kind of sports, as in a type of games

parts.note: to excel is to outdo
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone shines, winning gold at a sports event.
explanation.definitionFit: Games played in the open air are one kind of sports, so the adjective classifies them.

clue.text: A bit of land is granted to a tenant

parts.note: a property let is rented out to a tenant

explanation.surface: A plot of ground is leased to a tenant farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island is a little piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: A somewhat bald description

parts.note: 'bald' reads as blunt or plain, but it describes a balding head

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for having little hair on the crown, partly bald.

clue.text: The first runs come from straight strokes in cricket match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
in cricket, drives are straight batting strokes

explanation.surface: The opening runs of a game come from straight drives.
explanation.walkthrough: Runs is a cricket term in the surface, but defines trial outings in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial outing in a car before buying is a first run of it.

clue.text: Subject for those who have the mind to study

definitions.text: Subject for those who have the mind to study

parts.words: Subject for those who have the mind to study
parts.note: 'have the mind to' reads as being inclined, but the subject is the mind itself

explanation.definitionFit: The academic discipline whose subject matter is the mind and behaviour.

clue.text: It can be just a question of time

definitions.text: It can be just a question of time

parts.words: It can be just a question of time
parts.note: the phrase 'question of time' reads as inevitability, but the clue is a literal question asking the hour

explanation.walkthrough: An old-fashioned jocular way to ask what time it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated humorous phrase used to ask the time, a question about the hour.

clue.text: I'd turn up in a sort of orange fabric

indicators.note: the turned piece goes inside the rearranged colour word
a sort of orange is the colour word in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece is read upwards, reversing it

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, giving I and D

explanation.surface: Someone appears dressed in an orange-ish cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' rearranges the colour into ORGANE, and 'turn up' turns the contraction round so that 'in' can place it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine, stiff, translucent cotton muslin, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Variable income restricts business that could make a profit

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hem in the business piece
variable means changeable, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
CO, company, is a business

explanation.surface: Fluctuating earnings hold back a firm that might turn a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variable' rearranges the letters of the earnings word, and 'restricts' has them hold the firm abbreviation inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic venture is one that pays its way, able to generate a profit.

clue.text: See danger getting involved with traitors

indicators.note: involved means tangled, signalling the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Spot the peril of mixing with turncoats.
explanation.definitionFit: Renegades are deserters who abandon their side, so traitors.

clue.text: Notts opener wasn't well caught

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ailed means was unwell

explanation.surface: Nottinghamshire's opening batsman was ill and got caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts is Nottinghamshire, an English county cricket team; 'opener' looks like a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a criminal is to catch them, so nailed is a synonym of caught.

clue.text: Aimless ramble encountered in Low Church

parts.note: a cow lows, making a moo

explanation.surface: A wandering stroll ends up at a Low Church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Low Church is the evangelical wing of Anglicanism, but low is the cow's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooch is a slow purposeless wander, an aimless ramble.

clue.text: Many caught in a lie show spite

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many

indicators.note: the caught piece sits inside the words a lie

parts.note: taken as written
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Lots of people caught in a lie show nastiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns name ill will, the wish to hurt someone, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Coming from China, it is bottled in Italy

indicators.note: the answer comes out of these letters, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Although from China, it is bottled in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tuscan red wine, which is bottled in Italy.

clue.text: Student caught with a dictionary

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A pupil is caught with a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: A coed is an American term for a female student at a mixed college.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiefly American, a female student at a co-educational college.

clue.text: Bribe with hand lotion?

definitions.meaning: to palm someone is to bribe them, so the oil greasing a palm is a bribe
a whimsical reading of oil for the palm of the hand

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a bribe or payoff, and an oil from palm trees humorously read as hand cream.

clue.text: It's not fully-grown, anyway

parts.note: reads as a casual remark about a young animal; the insect stage between larva and adult is not fully grown either way

explanation.walkthrough: The young dog in its first three letters adds to the playful sense that this creature is not grown, anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect in its chrysalis stage, not yet an adult form.

clue.text: Something fragrant returned in the time left

indicators.note: the hidden letters are read backwards
the answer is concealed inside the words

explanation.surface: A scent comes back in the time remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin used in varnishes and perfume.

clue.text: Looking forward to being a member of the club?

definitions.text: being a member of the club?
definitions.meaning: 'in the club' is British slang for pregnant

explanation.definitionFit: Both anticipating and, colloquially, pregnant, two senses of one word.
